page.desc: 40,000 mAh laptop power banks compared on measured delivered watt-hours, watts from one USB-C port, weight and refill time, with prices read Nov 26, 2026 and the airline rule.
page.answer: Short answer. The best 40000mAh power bank for a laptop is the AOHi Starship 40000mAh 140W: ChargerLAB measured 121.6 Wh delivered at 100W from its 146 Wh, at 916 g. UGREEN's 48000mAh 300W costs less but weighs 1.65 kg. Both are over 100 Wh, so flying needs airline approval.

page.after:
What the differences mean

Why 40,000 mAh is the line. A bank this size holds 144 to 154 Wh, which is over the 100 Wh a passenger can fly with unasked. The TSA allows up to two spare lithium batteries of 101–160 Wh per person only with airline approval, in carry-on bags and never in checked ones. So this is a desk, car, cabin or campsite size, bought for close to two charges of a 14-inch laptop. Every row is 40,000 mAh or more as its maker labels it and has a USB-C port of at least 100 W. Omnicharge's Omni 40+ is left out for being just short: its maker lists 38,400 mAh (142 Wh).

  • Delivered energy, AOHi. ChargerLAB drained the Starship 40K at 20 V 5 A and counted 121.6 Wh. 121.6 ÷ 146 = 83% of the label. At 28 V 5 A it gave 116.52 Wh: 116.52 ÷ 146 = 80%.
  • Delivered energy, UGREEN. Macworld recharged a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro 1.8 times, and Apple rates that battery at 69.6 Wh. 1.8 × 69.6 = 125.3 Wh, and 125.3 ÷ 153.6 = 82%. Counting laptop recharges is a looser method than a bench load, so read this as approximate.
  • The mAh labels are on different scales. 153.6 Wh ÷ 48 Ah = 3.2 V, the LiFePO4 cell voltage; 146 Wh ÷ 40 Ah = 3.65 V. 153.6 ÷ 146 = 1.05, so 20% more mAh on the box is 5% more energy. Compare watt-hours, not mAh.
  • Weight per delivered watt-hour. 916.2 g ÷ 121.6 Wh = 7.5 g for the AOHi; 1,650 g ÷ 125 Wh = 13.2 g for the UGREEN. That is 1,650 − 916 = 734 g more to carry for about 4 Wh more.
  • Hours. ChargerLAB timed the AOHi at 1 h 29 min on a 100 W load, 2 h 42 min at 45 W and 1 h 3 min at 140 W.
Your useWhich fits
One laptop, and the bank gets carried (bag, car, campsite){buy:aohi-starship-40000mah-140w}, {after:aohi-starship-40000mah-140w} through our link: about the same laptop energy at 56% of the weight (916 ÷ 1,650)
Two or three laptops at a desk, or the lower price{buy:ugreen-48000mah-300w-power-bank}, {price:ugreen-48000mah-300w-power-bank}: three USB-C ports at 100 W each (Macworld), where ChargerLAB measured the AOHi at 62 W + 32 W on two
Longest service lifeThe UGREEN: LiFePO4 cells, with 80% capacity after 3,000 cycles as UGREEN's own claim (reported by Android Central)
A 16-inch MacBook Pro at full speedEither: both have one 140 W PD 3.1 port. ChargerLAB read 132.11 W from the AOHi into a 16-inch MacBook Pro (M4 Pro)
Flying without asking the airlineNeither. Stay under 100 Wh with a 25,000 mAh (90 Wh) bank such as {buy:ugreen-145w-25000mah-3-port-power-bank}

Both prices were read on Nov 26, 2026, in Black Friday week, and can change after Nov 30.

What was measured, and by whom

Dealectric does not test units. These are named reviewers' figures.

  • AOHi, other readings (ChargerLAB). It took 135 W at peak while refilling and reached 50% in 32 minutes. The case reached 39.6 °C after 30 minutes at 140 W. USB-C1 is input only, so two USB-C ports and one 20 W USB-A port feed devices. A USB-C cable marked 140 W is in the box.
  • UGREEN (Macworld, Simon Jary, July 17, 2024). It took the 14-inch MacBook Pro from 5% to 90% in an hour: 85% × 69.6 Wh = 59 Wh in 60 minutes.
  • UGREEN (Android Central, Harish Jonnalagadda, June 24, 2024). It refilled in just over 100 minutes and ships with one 240 W USB-C cable. He lists the weight as 4.1 lb (1.8 kg), heavier than Macworld's figure. His 55% efficiency compares the mAh the bank lost with the mAh of the phone battery it filled. A 3.2 V bank feeding a higher-voltage phone cell makes that ratio look worse than the energy loss is.

What your laptop asks for. Apple lists 140 W for fast-charging a 16-inch MacBook Pro, 96 W for the 14-inch and 70 W for a 2022 or later MacBook Air, so a 100 W port already covers the last two. For 140 W, Apple names a 240 W USB-C cable only for the 16-inch from Nov 2023 on; earlier 16-inch models need Apple's USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable. On either bank the 300 W or 140 W on the box does not change what one laptop gets: 140 W at most.

Not recommended right now: the CUKTECH 30

On Nov 26, 2026, cuktech.com showed the CUKTECH 30 as unavailable behind a $999.00 placeholder price, so it cannot be ordered from its maker. ChargerLAB's teardown found 28 V 5 A (140 W) on USB-C2 only; USB-C1 stops at 100 W, and the 300 W figure is the sum across ports. The three reviews read here (The Gadgeteer, Cult of Mac, MacSources) ran no discharge test, so its 144 Wh is a rated figure. It also weighs 1,130 g against the AOHi's 916 g for about the same rated energy.

The Techsmarter 40,000 mAh 100 W rugged bank is not in the table. Its maker's store returned no spec sheet or price to us on Nov 26, 2026, so there is no sourced watt-hour or weight figure to rank it on.
